title: Equal vs. Equitable Tutoring
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Compare an equal split of 45 tutoring hours with an equitable one by finding the allocation that brings three students to a score of 80.

educational.topic: Equality and equity in allocating support
learningObjectives: The learner will distinguish an equal allocation of tutoring hours from an equitable allocation by finding the split of 45 hours that brings all three students to a score of 80, and by stating the score gap that results from each.
prerequisites: Achievement gap, educational equity, equality, and learning gains, from Chapter 3.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Calculate, then search for the allocation that closes the gap
keyQuestions: How many students reach the target with an equal split?
Which allocation matches hours to need?
commonMisconceptions: Treating everyone the same is always fair
Equity means taking resources from students who are doing well
Equity requires giving everyone the same outcome by any means
assessmentOpportunities: What is the score gap with 15 hours each?
Which allocation brings all three students to 80?
Is treating everyone the same always fair?

controls.name: Q1 and Q2 boxes
controls.description: Type how many students reach 80 and the score gap under the equal split.

controls.name: Check Q1 and Q2
controls.description: Checks both answers and unlocks the hour sliders.

controls.name: Hours for A, B, C
controls.description: Set each student's tutoring hours from 0 to 45 in steps of 5. The total cannot exceed 45.

controls.name: Submit allocation
controls.description: Checks whether all three students reach 80. Three submissions are allowed.
